samples.summary: New `default:` throw in `format()` fires *after* side effects at the ~12 unvalidated `output()` call sites; only status/ctx/schema validate `--format` up front
samples.evidence: formatter.ts:51-55 now throws `InvalidFormatError` from `format()` for any value outside json|table|csv. Only the three commands touched by this diff call `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` before doing work; every other caller still passes the raw `opts.format` straight into `output()` after the request has already been executed (api-keys.ts:20 `output(res.data, opts.format, false)` after `createApiKey`, cells.ts:66/92/139 after writes, sheets-import.ts:91 after the import, docs/slides/notes create/update). With e.g. `wafflebase api-keys create ci --format jsonl`, the key is created server-side, `format()` throws, `outputError` prints INVALID_FORMAT and sets `process.exitCode = 1` — so a command that succeeded reports failure, and for `api-keys create` the raw key (shown only once, per the comment on line 19) is destroyed with no way to recover it. An agent seeing exit 1 will reasonably retry the mutation, duplicating writes. The guard added in this change (parseOutputFormat before any work) is exactly the right shape but was applied to only 3 of the call sites.

read api-keys.ts, cells.ts, sheets-import.ts, sheets-export.ts, docs.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts action bodies

samples.summary: `cell()`'s object-serialization fix is applied only to the single-record path; the array path still renders nested values as `[object Object]`
samples.evidence: table.ts:7-10 introduces `cell()` so nested values are JSON-serialized instead of stringified, and the doc comment claims parity with `formatCsv`. But the array branch (lines 46 and 53) still uses `String(row[k] ?? '')` for both width computation and rendering, so any array payload with a nested field (`schema` list rows, docs/cells responses with object fields) under `--format table` still prints `[object Object]` — and the widths are computed from that same wrong string, so switching one but not the other would also misalign columns. The stated defect is only half fixed.

samples.summary: Multi-line values break key/value table alignment in the new `formatRecord`
samples.evidence: formatRecord joins rows with '\n' and pads only the key column; a value containing a newline (e.g. an error `message`, a serialized nested object with embedded newlines, or a workspace name with a newline) produces continuation lines with no key padding, so the rendered table is silently misaligned/ambiguous. `cell()` does not escape newlines, unlike `formatCsv`'s quoting (csv.ts:20-23).

verdict.reason: Verified independently: format() throws InvalidFormatError in its default branch (formatter.ts:51-55) and output() calls it before printing (formatter.ts:59-62), so an invalid --format aborts rendering after the side effect. Only status.ts:64, schema.ts:21 and ctx.ts:73 call parseOutputFormat; a repo-wide grep found no other call sites and no indirect guard — the global --format option in root.ts:53 has no .choices()/parser, getGlobalOpts (root.ts:24-27) does no narrowing, and there are no commander preAction/hook wrappers anywhere in packages/cli/src. api-keys.ts:17-20 awaits createApiKey then passes the raw opts.format to output(), so `--format jsonl` creates the key server-side, throws before the once-only raw key is printed (comment at api-keys.ts:19), and the catch at 21-23 sets exit 1 on a request that actually succeeded. Same unguarded post-mutation pattern at cells.ts:66/92/139, sheets-import.ts:91, docs.ts:104/118/136/154, notes.ts:64/78/96/114, slides.ts:69/83/101/119. Tests (test/status.test.ts:168/181/230) cover INVALID_FORMAT only for the three validated commands, corroborating the gap. No counterexample exists.
